metadata.title: Basic Arithmetic Recall Quiz – Model Switch Smoke Test (TST101)
metadata.instructions: Answer each question in 1–3 sentences. Each question carries 1 mark. Write your answer clearly; no calculations need to be shown.

questions.question_text: According to the syllabus, what is the combined percentage for the activity labeled "Analyze"?

assessment.generation_notes: Questions are derived directly from the percentage data in Source 2 and Source 4 of the provided syllabus document, ensuring alignment with CO1 and the Remember Bloom level.

strengths: Both questions have clear, concise wording and are directly answerable from the syllabus.
Answer keys are indicated as present for each question.
Each question is mapped to a specific Course Outcome (CO1) and marks are evenly allocated.
weaknesses: All items are at the Remember level; no higher-order Bloom levels (Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create) are represented.
Both questions are Easy difficulty, providing no challenge variation for learners.
The assessment covers only CO1, leaving other potential Course Outcomes unassessed.
Total marks (2) are extremely low for a 20‑minute quiz, limiting the ability to differentiate student performance.
suggestions: Introduce at least one Apply‑level scenario question to move beyond simple recall.
Add an Analyze or Evaluate question that requires students to interpret or critique the syllabus percentages.
Include a Create‑level task (e.g., design a mini‑assessment plan) to achieve full Bloom coverage.
Diversify difficulty by adding a Medium or Hard question to better gauge depth of understanding.
Consider incorporating items mapped to additional COs to ensure broader curriculum alignment.
reviewer_result.reviewer_notes: The quiz functions as a basic factual check but does not fulfill OBE principles of assessing varied cognitive levels or multiple outcomes. Substantial redesign is recommended to improve academic rigor and alignment.
